title: Accepted Water-Thermal Provenance Binding
scope: owner-side provenance identity binding and accepted-receipt authorization only

invariants.assessment: Uses the single canonical F-KT transaction authority and adds no alternate kernel.
Production module contains no files, paths, parsing, formats or unit I/O.
Provenance metadata remains separate from physical water state, thermal state, forcing, numerical configuration and results.
Adds no persistent physical column state and duplicates no mass or temperature payload.
Adds no solver scratch, Jacobian or temporary numerical workspace to column state.
All provenance tokens are fixed-size scalar metadata with O(1) validation.
Trial identity originates from opaque F-KT candidates and accepted authorization requires the existing post-commit F-MR18 receipt.
Pure identity capture and comparison introduce no physical mutation and do not obstruct retry or warm-start reuse.
Uses generic [t0,t1] candidate intervals and the existing numeric time-identity rule only.
No fixed coupling-window duration or day-boundary assumption is introduced.
Accepted provenance is directly reusable by coupled runtime composition without making coupling an external afterthought.
Groundwater head/flux interface semantics are unchanged; EB-I10 only guards provenance identity.
No mass is created, modified, thresholded or rebooked.
Interface-sensitivity transport is untouched and remains available through existing canonical contracts.
Adds constant-cost metadata checks and no additional SWAP solve or coupling iteration.
Primitive cost and storage are O(1), but end-to-end MultiSWAP throughput of future production callsite composition is not qualified here.
Contains no MODFLOW-cell, tile, fraction or one-to-one mapping assumption.
Contains no deep-vadose assumption or state.
No component water storage or transfer amount is changed, so transition mass accounting is not altered.
Depends on generic F-KT candidate provenance rather than a particular soil-water solver implementation.
Adds no duplicate process physics and reuses existing canonical transaction capability.
No HeadCalc internals or solver arrays are referenced.
Contains no physical option or numerical solver policy and therefore cannot silently alter physics.
Validation is fixed-cost scalar work with no unbounded retry or fallback path.
Reference mode and existing reference physics are untouched.
Explicit status codes diagnose provenance failures, but production runtime publication of these diagnostics is not qualified here.
Provenance metadata is created only when the future caller requests this optional composition.
The primitive leaves route and system composition to runtime/coupler code and does not encode external topology.
No midnight, one-day, file-format or direct-MODFLOW dependency is introduced.
This machine-readable audit explicitly evaluates all thirty architecture invariants.

hard_nonclaims: advective sensible heat or enthalpy calculation
